newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stocks end shade up in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Manila stocks end shade up in lacklustre trade.

text.p: An absence of market moving factors and mild apprehension over the second quarter performance of companies kept investors on the sidelines and left Manila stocks drifting on Tuesday, brokers said.
The main index ended up 7.39 points, or 0.26 percent, at 2,798.25.

"Except for trade deficit figures this morning, there was not much to look at ...we also have indications that second quarter earnings won't be that good," Noel Reyes, vice president for research at Anscor Hagedorn Securities said.
Brokers said they expected the market, now in its second week of consolidation, to remain dull for the rest of the week.

Citisecurities said an uptrend would depend on blue chips but their fate again would be linked to second quarter earnings. "In case these companies fail to resurrect their bloody bottomlines, it is unlikely that the Philippine market will experience major and sustainable upswing," it said in a report.
Property firm Empire East Land was among the few secondliners that gained on Tuesday.
Its share surged 40 centavos, or 14.29 percent, to 3.20 pesos on what some said was technical buying, while one broker said was a rumour of a takeover by a leading Filipino businessman.
Company officials were not immediately available for comment.
